key_insight: Specialized, physics-driven machine learning force fields are needed to accurately simulate complex materials dynamics beyond the near-equilibrium regime where universal models are strongest.
engineering_relevance: For atomistic modeling of interfaces, open systems, phase evolution, and fracture, the right force field must be chosen and validated against the specific observable of interest, not just general benchmark accuracy.
method: Review and compare design trade-offs in ML interatomic potentials
Assess four challenging use cases: electrified interfaces, open systems, multiphase evolution, and fracture
Emphasize observable-specific benchmarking and hardware-aware model design
evidence_signal: The paper synthesizes findings from demanding application contexts and benchmarks them against intended observables to show where pretrained equivariant models fail under out-of-distribution dynamics.
watch_item: High-order or overly general architectures can be computationally expensive and still miss reactive or nonlocal physics, so specialization may improve accuracy but can reduce transferability.
paper_title: Specialized machine learning force fields for materials dynamics
